observations: No training logs or model hyperparameters were provided, so overfitting, convergence, and parameter suitability cannot be assessed. The combined five-factor model achieved IC 0.015196 versus SOTA 0.001834, an absolute improvement of 0.013362; annualized excess return after costs rose from 0.056066 to 0.086763, an improvement of 0.030697. Maximum drawdown improved from -0.082008 to -0.054514, reducing drawdown magnitude by 0.027494, so the current result dominates SOTA across all reported metrics.
hypothesis_evaluation: The results support the hypothesis that the implemented static MOM20, REV5, LOWVOL20, VOLSURPRISE20, and CLV1 factor set has useful combined predictive and portfolio value. However, because only combined results are reported, this run does not verify the efficacy or incremental contribution of each individual factor.
new_hypothesis: The performance improvement arises from complementary signals across medium-term momentum, short-term reversal, volatility, volume surprise, and intraday close location rather than from every factor contributing independently. Factor-level ablations and interaction-aware models should identify a smaller or dynamically weighted subset with stronger out-of-sample risk-adjusted performance.
reason: The approximately 8.29-fold IC increase, 54.75% gain in annualized excess return, and 33.53% reduction in drawdown magnitude indicate stronger predictive content with improved risk behavior.
